title: Design of a Biocompatible Drug-Eluting Tracheal Stent in Mice with Laryngotracheal Stenosis
protocol: Prepare two glass vials containing 70:30 PLLA-PCL polymer solutions.
Add 6 mg of rapamycin to one vial and 600 mg of 70:30 PLLA-PCL in another glass vial (control).
Add 6 mL of dichloromethane to each glass vial under a fume hood.
Add 120 μL of glycerol to each glass vial for increased flexibility and decreased stiffness.
Allow the solutions to dissolve and homogenize for 6−12 h.
Pipette 1 mL of rapamycin-containing PLLA-PCL solution into a glass Petri dish.
Allow the 70:30 PLLA-PCL solution containing 1% rapamycin to harden into a flat disk in the glass Petri dish.
Place the hardened disk in 2 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS, pH 7.4) and incubate in a 37 °C chamber.
Collect and replace PBS (2 mL) every 24 hours.
Use collected PBS for high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) analysis of rapamycin content.
Run samples through the autosampler injector along with serial dilutions of rapamycin to create a calibrated standard curve.
Run each sample in triplicate.
Prepare PLLA-PCL solutions containing rapamycin as described.
Use a glass Pasteur pipette with a rubber balloon to apply 1 mL of PLLA-PCL solution containing 1% rapamycin onto the venous cannula of a 22 G fluorinated ethylene propylene based angiocatheter.
Hold the angiocatheter in one hand and use the glass pipette to drop the PLLA-PCL solution onto the angiocatheter.
Slowly rotate the angiocatheter to ensure homogeneous coverage with the PLLA-PCL solution.
Prop the molded angiocatheter with its tip facing downward on the edge of a glass Petri dish for drying.
Allow stents to dry for 24 hours in a vacuum hood at room temperature.
Remove the stent construct from the underlying angiocatheter by gently twisting and sliding it out.
Check the stent circumferentially for any defects that may have occurred during casting.
Discard stents with defects.
Trim each end of the casted stent with fine straight scissors to ensure axial edges.
Cut 3 mm axial segments of the cast stent for use in a mouse model of LTS.
Anesthetize a 9-week old male C57BL/6 by giving an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (80−100 mg/kg) and xylazine (5−10 mg/kg).
Place a mouse on a surgical platform in a supine position.
Extend the cervical spine by looping a small loop of thread around the central incisors.
Affix the hands and legs of the mouse to the table using tape.
Pinch mouse paw to ensure adequate anesthesia.
Prep the surgical site.
Remove the overlying fur from the surgical area.
Clean the skin three times using an alternating iodine or chlorhexidine scrub with alcohol or diluted skin disinfectant.
Drape the area and wear sterile gloves.
Lay sterilized instruments on a sterile surface when not in use.
Make a 1.5 cm midline vertical incision in the neck of the mouse using fine curved iris scissors.
Divide the overlying thymus to lateralize the two resulting lobes for trachea visualization.
Bilaterally divide the sternohyoid and sternothyroid muscles at their superior attachment.
Pass a 22 G angiocatheter transorally through the larynx into the trachea.
Use small forceps to apply pressure to the anterior larynx of the mouse to assist in correct catheter placement.
Visualize the white angiocatheter through the trachea to ensure it is not placed in the esophagus.
Pass a bleomycin-coated wire brush through the inserted angiocatheter.
Slowly withdraw the angiocatheter so that only the wire brush remains in the trachea.
Apply counter pressure using fine forceps on the trachea to disrupt the lumen with the wire brush.
Reinsert the angiocatheter into the trachea over the wire brush.
Remove the wire brush and reapply bleomycin.
Repeat steps 4.8−4.12 a total of 5 times.
Apply bleomycin to the brush between each application.
Load one 3 mm casted stent onto an empty 22 G angiocatheter.
Draw a thin black vertical line on the 3 mm casted stent.
Transorally intubate the mouse with the angiocatheter that has been preloaded with the stent.
Visualize the stent on the angiocatheter in the trachea through the transcervical incision.
Hold the stent in place by gripping the trachea through the transcervical incision with fine forceps.
Remove the angiocatheter transorally while maintaining a grip on the stent with the fine forceps.
Do not apply excessive force to the stent when removing the angiocatheter.
Ensure sufficient force is applied to prevent the stent from being removed with the angiocatheter.
Use a 0.8 mm sialendoscope to visualize and confirm the location of the stent in the trachea.
Close the transcervical incision using tissue glue.
Allow each mouse to recover fully before returning it to its cage.
Anesthetize mice with an inhaled anesthetic for sacrifice by cervical dislocation according to the animal protocol.
Position a mouse on the surgical platform as previously described.
Reopen the neck incision using fine curved iris scissors.
Expose the trachea, following previous steps.
Divide the distal trachea below the level of the stent with fine curved iris scissors.
Divide the proximal trachea below the larynx and above the stent with fine curved iris scissors.
Separate the divided trachea from the esophagus posteriorly.
Remove the trachea, including the retained stent, from the mouse.
Fix the removed stent in 10% formalin for 24 hours.
Embed formalin-fixed mouse trachea specimens in paraffin with the distal end oriented superiorly.
Cut 5 μm sections of the paraffin-embedded mouse trachea using a microtome.
Deparaffinize the slides by placing them in xylene twice for 3 min each.
Place the slides in 100% ethanol for 2 min.
Place the slides in 95% ethanol for 2 min.
Place the slides in 70% ethanol for 2 min to rehydrate.
Wash the slides with running tap water for 2 min.
Stain the slides in hematoxylin for 3−5 min.
Wash the slides with running tap water for 5 min.
Place the slides in 1% acid alcohol for 1 min.
Wash the slides with running tap water for 1 min.
Rinse the slides in 0.2% ammonia water for 30 s.
Rinse the slides in running tap water for 5 min.
Dip the slides in 95% ethanol ten times.
Eosin stain by placing the slide in eosin phloxine for 30 s.
Dehydrate the slides by placing them in 95% ethanol for 5 min.
Place the slides in absolute ethanol twice for 5 min each.
Place the slides in xylene twice for 5 min.
Mount the slides with xylene-based mounting medium.
Prepare tissue sections as described in steps 6.1−6.4.
Do not remove stent from these tracheal sections to visualize changes in inflammation relative to the location of the stent within the lumen of the trachea.
Observe macrophage and T cell activity using CD3 and F4/80 markers.
Place 5 μm cut sections of paraffin-embedded trachea on hydrophilic plus slides.
Place each slide in xylene twice for 5 minutes each.
Place each slide in 100% ethanol twice for 3 minutes each.
Place each slide in 95% ethanol for 1 minute.
Immerse the slides in antigen retrieval buffer and place them in a vegetable steamer with boiling water for 20 minutes.
Remove staining racks from the steamer, discard antigen retrieval buffer, and replace it with PBS.
Discard PBS after immersion of slides for 1 minute.
Incubate slides with DMEM containing 10% FBS for 30 minutes.
Discard DMEM and add a mixture of primary antibodies raised in different species to the slides.
Cover slides with paraffin film and incubate overnight at 4 °C in a dark room.
Wash the slides in PBS 3x for 5 min.
Incubate the slides with secondary antibodies diluted in DMEM with 10% FBS for 0.5−1 h at room temperature in the dark.
Wash the slides in PBS 3x for 5 min in the dark.
Mount the slides on coverslips with a drop of mounting medium containing DAPI.
Store the slides in the dark at either 20 °C or 4 °C.
Observe the stained slides on a laser scan confocal microscope and photograph.
Quantify the total number of cells staining with DAPI and antibodies of interest for comparison to uninjured trachea.
Collect mouse trachea as described in steps 6.1−6.7 and remove stent.
Desiccate the tracheal tissue using fine scissors.
Further homogenize the tracheal tissue using a bead mill homogenizer with 1.4 mm ceramic beads for one 40 s cycle at 6 m/s.
Extract RNA from tracheal lysate using a column-based extraction and purification kit following manufacturer's instructions.
Quantify RNA from each sample using a spectrophotometer.
Create complementary DNA from extracted RNA using reverse transcriptase.
Prime the reaction at 25 °C for 5 min.
Perform reverse transcription at 46 °C for 30 min.
Inactivate the reverse transcriptase at 95 °C for 1 min.
Dilute complementary DNA samples with RNase-free water to a concentration of 10−25 ng/mL.
Mix 1 µL of diluted complementary DNA with 10 µL of PCR mastermix.
Add 8 µL of ddH2O to the mixture.
Pipette 0.5 μL of each gene-specific forward and reverse primer into the mixture.
Ensure the total volume in each well is 20 μL.
Run each sample for each gene in triplicate.
Repeat steps for all genes of interest, including collagen 1, collagen 3, and β-actin.
Place the 96 well plate on the real-time quantitative PCR machine.
Initiate denaturation at 95 °C for 15 seconds.
Anneal and extend at 60 °C for 60 seconds.
Repeat the annealing and extending step for a total of 40 cycles.
Normalize the cycle threshold value (CT) for each gene of interest (GOI) to the CT value for the reference gene β-actin.
Calculate ΔCT for each GOI using the formula: ΔCT = CT (GOI) – CT (reference gene).
Determine ΔΔCT by subtracting the untreated sample's ΔCT from the treated sample’s ΔCT.
Calculate the relative change in gene expression as an expression of fold change using 2ΔΔCT.
